newsitem.title: UK: US Stocks in mixed in London, focus on technology.
newsitem.headline: US Stocks in mixed in London, focus on technology.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mixed in light trading in London on Wednesday, with interest focused on the technology sector, after Motorola Inc posted better-than-expected earnings and Advanced Micro Devices Inc fell short of profit expectations, dealers said.
"It's a mixed bag and very much a technology story," said one London dealer.
Shares in Motorola, which released its results after Wall Street closed, rose $1-3/4 in London to $84-1/2, having gained $2-3/16 in New York on Tuesday.
Shares in AMD, the computer chip maker, tumbled $3 to $36. The shares closed $1-1/8 higher in New York on Tuesday, before AMD released its profits.
Losses in AMD spilled over into the sector, pushing most other technology shares down.
Shares in Intel Corp, AMD's main competitor, eased $3/8 to $149-1/4 amid concerns about price pressures.

Among others in the sector, shares in Texas Instruments Inc lost $3/8 to $91-5/8, while shares in International Business Machines Corp slipped $1/4 to $95-1/4. Shares in Digital Equipment Corp were unchanged at $37-1/8.

"Motorola is the big headline stock and its earnings may help overall sentiment on Wall Street, but it could fade fast," a dealer said. "This market will be earnings-driven for the next couple of weeks."
Dealers said they expected Wall Street to open a bit higher. September S&P 500 futures were up 1.20 points at 929.00 on Globex at 1045 GMT and September long bond futures were up 1/32 to 113-21/32.

In other trading, dealers said shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc slipped $1/8 to 44-1/4 on a Washington Post report that said the White House would reject a key element of the proposed $368 billion tobacco settlement because it would impose new restrictions on federal authority to regulate nicotine in cigarettes.
Shares in McDonald's Corp added $1/4 to $49 after a Wall Street Journal report said the fast-food chain was to name five new division presidents to be responsible for increasing domestic business.
Dealers said gains in the shares were capped by the belief that McDonalds' internal problems may be months away from being solved. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
